title: Silksong is getting a free expansion in 2 weeks
content: In a "Cherry Time!" presentation , Hollow Knight developer Team Cherry has just revealed a first look at its much-anticipated first content update to Hollow Knight: Silksong. The nautical-themed Sea of Sorrow will come as a free update on December 11. Team Cherry said that Sea of Sorrow will contain multiple new areas, power-ups, and bosses, while I clocked at least three new friendly NPCs in the trailer: A townsperson, a new shopkeeper, and a ferryman. Area-wise, I made out three distinct tilesets in the trailer: A rain-blasted fishing town on the water, a harrowing climb with an electrical storm element, and a green space reminiscent of the early game Bell Bottom. At least the first of these areas appears to be built on cut content for Silksong: "Pharloom Bay" is well-documented on the Hollow Knight wiki , and would have been located on the east side of the map, near the thematically-similar Greymoor. Some elements in the trailer correspond to ones documented by the wiki, like an underwater submersible vehicle, or a scientific lab in the electrical storm area. Which all sounds rad to me, particularly the submersible. Among the all-timer videogame level concepts, "underwater techbase" is one of my very favorites, and Team Cherry seem to be approaching these concepts with a Lovecrafty, Innsmouth flair that reminds me of the Fishing Village zone from Bloodborne. Silksong is already a massive game, and I'm curious as to how Sea of Sorrow will fit both the map, and the game's overall flow from act to act. We'll find out for sure when the free expansion releases on December 11. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together

title: Vermintide 2 mod tools get a public release, and the game's 90% off on Steam too
summary: Holy Sigmar, bless this ravaged body.
content: Though Vermintide 2's had a Steam Workshop since 2018, it's mostly used for quality-of-life stuff like UI tweaks. That's set to change now that Fatshark has announced a public release of its internal developer tools, which they say "will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more!" Right now, only a select number of sanctioned mods can be used in Vermintide 2's "official realm" which is the one with loot and leveling that carries over, while unsanctioned mods can only be accessed in a "modded realm" where there are no progression systems. Obviously that's off-putting to a lot of players, so Fatshark has announced a change. "We have an update releasing in early December which will see the Modded Realm have its own, local, offline progression. That means that playing in the Modded Realm will still result in you gaining loot and experience, but said progression will not reflect on the Official Realm. This should make playing on the Modded Realm feel much better and not be discouraging for those that want to try out all of the unsanctioned mods, both the ones that already exist and the ones to come thanks to the Mod Tools!" I'm not sure how many players will be happy to start over from level one just to get access to a wider variety of mods, but I hope it encourages some folks to check them out. Another thing that'll encourage new players is that XP has been doubled from now through till Monday, and Vermintide 2 is on sale for 90% off on Steam . The DLC has been discounted too. In less good news, the servers for Versus Mode are being turned off. "We have monitored the use of the dedicated Versus servers lately," Fatshark said, "and come to the conclusion that they are barely used. We have therefore decided to shut these down." Versus Mode will still be playable, but via the menu option for a custom game or the lobby browser. You'll have to find a crew to play with on Discord first, which is how everyone seems to play Versus at the moment anyway. That shutdown is planned for early December, at the same time as the update that adds local progression to the modded realm. That update will also include balance changes to buff some unpopular talents, new weapon icons, and a Tome of Triumphs in the hub area that will point you at any event if there's a live one, or to the weekly event mode if there isn't. The next event planned is the annual return of Gifts of the Wolf Father in December. Finally, Fatshark mentioned that focusing on the mod tools to get them ready for public release had to take priority from other updates. "The weapon pack and the level that we mentioned in the past has been put on hold," they wrote. "We still want to get back to that, especially the weapon pack, but for now there is no active development on that. It’s important for us that we have transparency here, and while we are not working on these things, we do stick with our games! We have plans both near and far for Vermintide 2." title: Witcher 3 Remastered patch has lighting fixes, sign nerfs, and gets rid of a nasty werewolf bug
summary: Turns out they weren't meant to be that hard to kill after all.
content: If you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny new remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02 . "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too quickly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat." Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering." That's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version launched with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play. I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC . They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun. Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last. title: Physical media is cool again, baby, so drop the needle on some videogame vinyls this Black Friday
summary: Music you can hold in your hands!
content: I am an absolute sucker for physical media—my bookshelves are adorned with generations of console games, I have a CD stash tucked away in my Mum's attic, and I still refuse to buy a Kindle in favour of good ol' fashioned paper and ink. And as we increasingly veer into a more digital age, I've noticed a huge uptick in people yearning to bring their hobbies and collections back into a more tangible form. Music, especially, has seen a huge resurgence in physical popularity. Y'all, my best friend is buying CDs and ripping them onto his PC. Like the good old days! And we've also seen an increasing number of videogame soundtracks make their way onto CD and vinyl, which is something that I am a huge fan of. I love music. I love videogames. I love things I can hold in my hands. It's a triple win! We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here Unfortunately, this Black Friday hasn't brought about a ton of good deals on videogame vinyl. But that doesn't mean there aren't little offers to be found here and there. So if you're fixing to expand your physical media collection—or seeking out a gift for the videogame music lover in your life—I've got you covered. If you're looking to scoop up a few albums at once, Target is currently doing a Buy 2 Get 1 Free deal on all its music. It's got a pretty tasty library of videogame OSTs among its 49 pages of soundtrack music, such as: Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI: the Album C418 Minecraft Volume Alpha Jagex Audio Team Runescape: 25 Years Andrew Jeremy Coffee Talk (original Soundtrack) From Software Bloodborne (original Soundtrack) Jeremy Soule The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (original Soundtrack) Clint Mansell Doom (original Soundtrack) D'Anthoni Wooten Dave the Diver (original Soundtrack) Bethesda Softworks Deathloop (original Soundtrack) Martin O'Donnell Halo 3 (original Soundtrack) Piotr Musial Frostpunk 2 (original soundtrack) Valve Studio Orchestra Fight Songs: The Music of Team Fortress 2 If you're looking for straight-up discounts, that's a little bit of a tougher find. IAm8Bit is doing a small sale on its collection of vinyls, offering between $5 and $15 off some stellar soundtracks like: Machine Girl Neon White Soundtrack Part 1 Studio MDHR Cuphead: The Delicious Last Course Ben Babbitt Kentucky Route Zero Vinyl is still pretty expensive, but hey. If you're clever with your selections at Target you can easily nab a $40 - $50 vinyl for free, and IAm8Bit have great indie options for some bonus purchases that are also a tad cheaper.

title: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
summary: Just think what you'll be able to do with those extra 156 KB they're freeing up.
content: In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release." This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers. By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana . A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.
